passage: At the art table in Class One, Keerthana leaned over to look at the picture beside hers. Sahil had drawn a sun with long, wavy rays and a tiny bird on a wire. "Your drawing is so good!" she said, and felt a smile spread on her own face. She looked at her own sun, which was just a yellow circle. "Will you show me how you did the rays?" Sahil grinned and handed her his crayon. "Start with a line, then wiggle."

qa.q: What did Sahil draw on a wire?
qa.a: He drew a tiny bird on a wire.

qa.q: How did Keerthana feel when she told Sahil his drawing was good?
qa.a: She felt happy to give kind words. Her spreading smile and her wish to learn from him show admiration without envy.

qa.q: Why was asking "Will you show me?" a wise next step?
qa.a: It turned admiration into learning, and Sahil could share what he knows. She gets better at drawing rays and they both enjoy it. 😊

qa.q: How might Sahil feel when Keerthana praises his picture and asks for help?
qa.a: He probably feels proud and glad to be asked. He grinned and gave her a crayon, so he seems happy to share the trick.

grounding: I tell my friend his drawing is so good, feel happy and ask him to show me how.
